messages:
Alex: heads-up — we just saw a flurry of keystore decrypt failures in eu-west-1, lots of GPU node boot loops. looks like model weights couldn't be decrypted so pods keep restarting.
Maya: saw that alert. logs show: `keystore: decrypt error: 429 RATE_EXCEEDED` from the keystore-proxy when many nodes try to decrypt on boot.
Tom: did anything change in the egress rules this morning? I remember a tight firewall rollback earlier.
Priya: yep we tightened egress to the keystore subnet at 09:03 and added a DDoS ACL rule. trying to verify if that impacted connection reuse.
Alex: timeline: deploy at 08:55 -> firewall tightened 09:03 -> autoscaler added 40 nodes 09:10-09:25 -> keystore QPS spike -> 429s -> node boot loops 09:12 onwards.
Erin-oncall: paging SRE — this is causing sustained provisioning backlog and autoscaler keeps spinning/releasing nodes which is going to blow this hour's GPU spend.
ops-bot: autoscaler: launched 38 g4dn nodes (eu-west-1) between 09:10-09:24; terminated 27 due to failed healthchecks.
deploy-bot: can confirm: rollout of infra-policy-2026-03 completed at 09:03, no rollout rollbacks yet.
Maya: quick mitigation idea: relax egress rules to allow port 8443 to keystore-proxy and add ephemeral NAT for warm pool subnet, then restart keystore-proxy in eu-west-1 with higher token cache TTL.
Tom: we should also add a local file-based transient cache on init so nodes don't hammer keystore on boot. short patch: `/etc/redwood/keystore-cache.conf` with ttl=120s, size=500.
Priya: creating a firewall rollback PR now — if we revert the ACL it should restore connection pooling and drop QPS on the keystore.
Alex: confirmed 429s correlate with concurrent decrypt attempts: sample error snippet from node:
```
2026-03-20T09:16:02Z keystore-proxy ERROR decrypt failed: status=429 message="Quota exceeded: keystore decrypt"
2026-03-20T09:16:02Z runtime WARN model-loader: decrypt_retry=0 -> abort
```
Maya: also noticed keystore-proxy logs show a burst of TLS handshake failures due to many short-lived connections; firewall change probably disabled keepalive/NAT timeouts.
Erin-oncall: rolling rollback approved. Priya — patch and rollback now, Priya hit me when it's in flight.
Priya: rolling back infra-policy-2026-03 now (PR #4128) -> applying to eu-west-1.
ops-bot: rollback started on eu-west-1 firewall at 09:29:22.
Alex: while rollback is in progress, please patch the keystore-proxy to increase internal decrypt cache: set `KEystore_CACHE_TTL=180` and `MAX_CONCURRENT_DECRYPT=200` in config and restart.
Tom: grabbing a small hotfix for the node image to seed a tiny on-disk cache before first decrypt. pushing image `redwood/node:2026-03-20-hotfix`.
Maya: quick cost note — autoscaler churn already increased GPU bill estimate for the hour by ~£3.2k per ops-bot calc. we should set temporary limit on scale-up to avoid repeating.
ops-bot: autoscaler: applying temporary cap `scale_up_limit=12` for eu-west-1 at 09:31.
Priya: rollback completed at 09:34:01. early signs: keystore-proxy handshake errors dropping.
Maya: after rollback and keystore-proxy restart, decrypt 429s dropped to near-zero by 09:39; gym of nodes started passing healthchecks.
Erin-oncall: marking incident as mitigated. follow-ups: keystore rate limits, egress keepalive policy, autoscaler backoff, node init caching. Need an RFC for graceful boot decrypt flow.
Alex: agree. immediate actions: 1) keep `scale_up_limit=12` for 2 hours 2) backfill node image hotfix 3) schedule keystore capacity increase or per-customer quota smoothing 4) firewall runbook update re: NAT keepalive.
Tom: I'll open a small PR to add on-disk seed cache + exponential backoff on decrypt attempts. Priya — can you add the firewall rollback steps to runbook?
Priya: adding runbook notes and tagging infra-ops for review. PRs: #4129 (node image), #4130 (keystore proxy config), #4131 (runbook).
Maya: cost breakdown snapshot from ops-bot: churned nodes 38->27 = 11 wasted node-hours ~ 0.6 GPU-hours after autoscaler billing rounding -> ~£3.2k estimate includes reserved capacity amortization. we'll reconcile with finance.
Erin-oncall: postmortem owner? Alex or Maya?
Alex: I'll take postmortem; will include timeline, telemetry queries, recommended changes. Target draft within 24h.
Tom: one more note — add circuit breaker logic to keystore client library so node init stops aggressive retries after N failures and delays to random jitter.
Maya: thanks all. closing thread once postmortem link is up. :thumbsup:
